title: Space bound for Word RAM decisions
statement: Let $P$ be an extended Word RAM program, $L$ a language of Boolean strings, and $W,T_W,S_W,F:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose a finite Turing machine computes $W(n)$ in at most $T_W(n)$ steps and space $S_W(n)$. Suppose that for every input $x$ there are a time bound $t$ and an output string $o$ such that $P$ halts within $t$ steps at word width $W(|x|)$, outputs the Boolean indicator of membership of $x$ in $L$, and touches at most $F(|x|)$ addresses. If for some natural number $a$ and function $s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, every $n$ satisfies $S_W(n)+F(n)(W(n)+1)+W(n)+(\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1)+1\le a s(n)$, then $L$ belongs to space $s$, that is, $L\in\mathrm{SPACE}(s)$.
hypotheses_covered: An extended Word RAM program $P$ and Boolean language $L$
A finite Turing machine computes $W(n)$ within time $T_W(n)$ and space $S_W(n)$
For every input, there are $t,o$ witnessing halting at width $W(|x|)$ with the membership indicator as output
